`Tooltip.test.ts` tests the root through the parts: the open state with each reason, `v-model:open` and `v-model:trigger-id`, `cancel()`, the dismissal, the hover, the focus, the press, `disabled`, `disableHoverablePopup`, `trackCursorAxis`, the group, `data-instant` and a trigger in a trigger. Vue has no `flushSync`, so the popup renders in the update after the hover event. The parts render no transition status and no unmount action: `<Transition>` animates the popup, and its JavaScript hooks replace `unmount()`, `preventUnmountOnClose()` and `openChangeComplete` (rule 8.9).

`Tooltip.test.ts` tests the handle and more triggers: triggers outside the root, `open(id)`, `close()`, `isOpen`, the payload of each trigger, a press on a trigger that is not active, a disabled trigger and the unmount of the active trigger. `Tooltip.hydration.test.ts` tests the server HTML of an open root. A trigger that is not active reads a `computed` of its own state, so it does not render again.

`Tooltip.test.ts` tests the trigger: its element and attributes, `data-popup-open`, `data-trigger-disabled`, the hover and its delay, the press, the focus after the window, `closeOnClick` and the error with no root.
`Tooltip.test.ts` tests the provider: its `delay`, its `closeDelay`, a trigger `delay` over the provider, and `timeout`, which keeps the group active after a close.

`Tooltip.test.ts` tests the popup: its element and attributes, its children, the hover on the popup, a popup that a `v-if` replaces and the error with no positioner. The parts render no transition status and no unmount action: `<Transition>` animates the popup, and its JavaScript hooks replace `unmount()`, `preventUnmountOnClose()` and `openChangeComplete` (rule 8.9).
`Tooltip.test.ts` tests the portal: `keepMounted` and `to`. The portal renders no element of its own, so its `render` and `className` have no element.

`Tooltip.test.ts` tests the positioner: the side `top`, the anchor at the pointer and `pointer-events: none` while the popup cannot be hovered. `Popover.test.ts` tests the placement of the shared layer.
`Tooltip.test.ts` tests the arrow: its element, `aria-hidden` and the attributes of its side.
`Tooltip.test.ts` tests the viewport: the id of the active trigger in its slot and the direction of a move. A `<Transition>` keyed by that id replaces `data-current` and `data-previous`.
`Tooltip.spec.ts` tests the types of the handle, the details, the props of the root, the trigger, the portal and the positioner, and the element of a template ref.
`Tooltip.spec.ts` tests the types of the handle, the details, the props of the root, the trigger, the portal and the positioner, and the element of a template ref.
`@after-enter` and `@after-leave` of a `<Transition>` around the popup run after its animations (rule 8.9).
A template ref of the root has `close()`. The `unmount` action is cut: with `:css="false"`, the `leave` hook of a `<Transition>` keeps the popup until it calls `done` (rule 8.9).
The portal is a `<Teleport>` and renders no element of its own, so it has no `render`, `as` and `element`. The developer writes an element in the portal when they need one.

The state has no `transitionStatus`, and the popup has no `data-starting-style`, `data-ending-style`, `data-open` and `data-closed`: `<Transition>` around the popup animates it, and a kept popup has `[hidden]` (rules 8.9 and 8.15). `class`, `style` and the `element` slot replace `className`, `style` and `render`.

The row gives the default `600`. The prop has no Vue default, because Base UI tells an absent prop from a number: an absent prop takes the delay of `Tooltip.Provider`. With no provider, the part uses 600 for an absent prop, which is the default that Base UI documents.

surfaceAdditions.reason: The state says that the tooltip does not open from this trigger, by its `disabled` prop or by the root. It is the source of `data-trigger-disabled` (rule 3). Base UI has no such state.
The part reads `id` to name the trigger in the root, so it is a declared prop. Base UI reads it from the native attributes of the trigger, and `types.md` has no row for a native attribute.
A disabled portal renders at its source, also on the server (VUE-128).
The portal is a `<Teleport>`, and it takes the props of `<Teleport>`: `defer` waits for the other content of the update.
`v-model:trigger-id` binds the active trigger, as a second state that a developer binds is a named model (rule 8.5).

returnTypeDifferences.reason: `Tooltip.Handle` is the class `TooltipHandle`. The declaration of the function names the class, and Base UI documents the same class by its name in the namespace.

relocations.behavior: The root holds the open state, the active trigger and the layer of the tooltip.

The state of the root: the open state, the active trigger, the reason and the instant state.
The open delay of a trigger with no `delay` and no provider: 600 ms.
The trigger opens the tooltip at a hover and at the focus of a key, and closes it at a press.
The provider gives one delay to the tooltips in it.
The group of the tooltips of a provider.
The portal renders its content in a `<Teleport>` after its mount.
The portal marks the parts in it.

The arrow points to the anchor.
